question.text: In the pulley system pictured, block 1 hangs from the fixed pulley and blocks 2 and 3 hang from the two ends of the string over the movable pulley. Block 3 accelerates downward at 6 m/s² and block 2 accelerates upward at 4 m/s². Determine the acceleration of block 1.
conditions: fixed pulley at top, block 1 hangs from it
movable pulley hangs below the fixed pulley, blocks 2 and 3 hang from its two ends

figure.description: A fixed pulley is mounted at the top, attached to a rigid support. A string runs over this fixed pulley: block 1 hangs from one end (the left side), and the other end connects to the axle of a second, movable pulley that hangs below it. A second string runs over this movable pulley, with block 2 hanging from its left end and block 3 hanging from its right end.

solution.approach: Use the movable-pulley constraint to find the pulley's acceleration from blocks 2 and 3, then use the fixed-pulley constraint to find block 1's acceleration.

steps.text: Take downward as positive. Block 3's acceleration is 6 m/s² downward and block 2's is 4 m/s² upward, so its downward value is −4 m/s².
The movable-pulley constraint makes the pulley's downward acceleration the average of the two.
The fixed-pulley constraint makes block 1's downward acceleration the negative of the movable pulley's.
A negative downward acceleration means block 1 actually accelerates upward.

common_mistakes.text: Taking block 1's acceleration in the same direction as the movable pulley instead of the opposite direction gives 1 m/s² downward, the wrong direction.
